Wasteland 2: Directors Cut from Wikipedia

In February 2015, the developers announced that the game will be receiving a visual upgrade with the game engine being moved to the Unity 5 from Unity 4.5 and new gameplay features will be added to the game which were announced to be revealed later. Also the modders would get new tools since Unity 5 contains many of the tools available in Unity 4.x Pro.

On March 3, 2015, at the Game Developers Conference Microsoft announced that Wasteland 2 was in development for Xbox One. The following day, Wasteland 2 was announced for PlayStation 4. The updated version will be titled Wasteland 2: Game of the Year Edition. The console version will be a port of the enhanced PC version of the game. In April 2015, the developers said that it will run at 1080p resolution on both consoles. The enhanced version will be available for free to all Kickstarter backers and anyone who bought the original game.

In May 2015, the release window of the enhanced edition was revealed to be during late summer of 2015. In June 2015, Wasteland 2: Game of the Year Edition was renamed to Wasteland 2: Director's Cut and a trailer showcasing the enhanced version was released on June 23, 2015.

Besides the visual upgrade the game also features many other improvements and additions. The edition contains expanded voice-overs with addition of over 8000 lines of pre-recorded dialogs. New gameplay features include new perks and quirks are available which add unique bonuses and characteristics. The "Precision Strike" system allows the player to target individual body parts to cripple or stun enemies, or shatter their armour. Additionally the enhanced edition also contains redesigned encounters, a redesigned user interface and a requisite controller support.
